assumptions: Cases use a fictional Loopwell project (brand guide and Feature map), a stubbed Search Console and stubbed model answers; tests/test_prompt_panel.py supplies them offline. They are not live evidence.
The keyword plan is not read: its keywords.json is larger than the 64 KB a code workflow can read, so the families come from Search Console alone.
cost_drivers: One Search Console read and one gpt-6-luna call of up to 32,000 input bytes and 4,096 output tokens; a second call only when check_panel lists failures. Unmeasured until qualification.
effects: Replaces reports/research/prompt-panel/PROMPT_PANEL.md when every check passes; the organic audit asks the newest such panel for its site. Never runs prompts against an AI assistant; no send, post, spend, PR or provider change.

cases.description: Loopwell: a brand guide naming the category and Search Console queries dominated by an adjacent category. The core family must lead.
No brand guide, Feature map or onboarding plan: the run stops and names the files instead of guessing the category.
The first answer has a discovery prompt that reads "which project management tool is best for early-stage startups": the check must catch it and the published panel must not contain it.

excludes: which project management tool is best for early-stage startups

rubric.question: Is F1 the category the positioning says the product sells in, in the buyers' own words, and does it weigh 0.40?
Do the prompts read like what people type into an assistant: short, varied, close to real queries, open and plural, with no invented budgets or team sizes?
Does the product appear only in the branded prompts, and is every competitor mention flagged?
